name: Delhi

localities.name: Dwarka
localities.intro: Dwarka's CGHS societies and DDA pockets run on gate-pass discipline — most managing committees want a move intimation at the society office a day or two before your date. Wide sector roads make 32-ft container access easy in most pockets, unlike inner Delhi.
highlights: Sector 4, 6, 10 and 12 CGHS societies typically require the resident to deposit a move form with the RWA before entry
Service lifts in taller towers (Sector 18B–23) are shared between two wings — early-morning slots go first
Bharat Vandana and Dwarka Expressway-adjacent sectors allow larger trucks right up to the gate in daylight hours

localities.name: Rohini
localities.intro: Rohini's plotted DDA colonies and co-op housing blocks are organised and comparatively easy for movers — but R-Zone and market-adjacent blocks get congested, so morning loading slots matter. Most RWAs here are used to move requests and process gate passes quickly.
highlights: Blocks facing the sector markets (Pocket B-4, B-5) often need the truck staged on the service lane
DDA flat staircases in older pockets are narrow — double-door fridges usually need a 3-man stair carry
Rohini West and Sector 24+ pockets have easier truck access than the Phase 1–2 inner blocks

localities.name: Lajpat Nagar
localities.intro: Lajpat Nagar moves are won or lost on parking: the central market lanes are effectively closed to trucks, and colonies allow loading from the main road in off-peak hours. Expect a shuttle tempo for anything beyond the ground-floor blocks facing the main roads.
highlights: Central Market and Feroze Gandhi Road pockets need a small shuttle vehicle between truck and door
Stationing a container on the Ring Road service lane is restricted — plan a 7–10 a.m. loading window
Builder floors without lifts are the norm — inventory multi-floor homes honestly to size the crew

localities.name: Karol Bagh
localities.intro: Karol Bagh's Ajmal Khan Road and Bank Street arteries are market-first, so household moves run on early mornings and back lanes. Older buildings mean small staircases and frequent no-lift carries — a pre-move survey genuinely changes the quote here.
highlights: Truck entry on market streets is impractical after 10 a.m. — loading starts by 7 a.m.
Many buildings have no service lift; budget stair-carry time on 2nd floor and above
Gaffar Market and Tank Road pockets usually need a two-stage shuttle move

localities.name: Mayur Vihar
localities.intro: Mayur Vihar Phase 1–3 societies sit between the Noida Link Road and the Yamuna — convenient for NCR moves, but each pocket's association has its own gate-pass drill. Phase 1's older CGHS blocks have tighter basements and ramps than the newer Phase 3 towers.
highlights: Pocket-level associations issue move passes; residents usually apply a day ahead at the society office
Phase 1 basement ramps are height-restricted — large containers stage on the main road
Peak-hour entry from the Noida side adds 30–45 minutes, so intercity loads are scheduled early

localities.name: Saket
localities.intro: Saket's mix of J-block builder floors, DDA pockets and gated enclaves like Saket Country Homes means access varies street by street. Moves near Press Enclave Road need off-peak staging; inner lanes are calm once you're off the main road.
highlights: Builder-floor blocks without lifts dominate J and DDA pockets — crew size follows floor count
Saidulajab and the MB Road stretch have better truck access than inner Saket lanes
Weekday mid-mornings are the practical window; evening market traffic blocks Press Enclave Road

localRules.title: Commercial-vehicle no-entry windows
localRules.detail: Most Delhi arterial roads bar medium and heavy goods vehicles during the morning and evening peaks — roughly 7–11 a.m. and 5–9 p.m. Loading and unloading are therefore planned for midday or early-morning slots, and your crew will confirm the workable window a day before the move.

localRules.title: GRAP winter restrictions
localRules.detail: Between October and January, GRAP stages can suspend diesel goods vehicles below BS-VI (and occasionally most diesel trucks) inside Delhi when air quality turns severe. If your move date is flexible, asking for a CNG/BS-VI vehicle during this period avoids last-minute rescheduling.

localRules.title: RWA gate passes
localRules.detail: Most organised colonies — Dwarka and Rohini CGHS societies, Gulmohar Park, Vasant Kunj pockets — expect a move intimation to the RWA or managing committee 24–48 hours ahead, along with the vehicle's registration number. Resident tenants should keep their landlord informed the same way.

localRules.title: Narrow-lane shuttle transfers
localRules.detail: Old Delhi, Karol Bagh, Lajpat Nagar's market lanes and parts of Shahdara cannot take a 32-ft container. The convention is a two-stage move: a small covered tempo shuttles between your door and the full-size truck staged on the nearest main road. This is quoted as a separate, visible line.

localRules.title: Parking and height barriers
localRules.detail: Service lanes on the Inner Ring Road and several colony entries have ~3.5 m height barriers that stop large containers. Crews check approach roads during the pre-move survey and pick the largest vehicle that can legally and physically reach your gate.

seasonality.peak: March–July and the last five days of every month
seasonality.note: Delhi's peak moving rush follows the school and job-transfer calendar: March to July is the busiest stretch, with month-ends tightest for truck availability. Winter moves are calmer but watch for GRAP-related vehicle restrictions after Diwali.

faqs.q: How is my moving quote calculated?
faqs.a: It depends on your inventory, floors, lift access, packing level and distance. We run a free survey (video or doorstep) and then confirm an itemised written quote — no advance is needed to book.

faqs.q: Can trucks enter my Delhi colony during the day?
faqs.a: Medium and heavy goods vehicles face peak-hour no-entry windows on most arterial roads (broadly 7–11 a.m. and 5–9 p.m.). We schedule loading for midday or early morning, and where a colony entry has a height barrier we bring the largest vehicle that fits.

faqs.q: Do you handle society or RWA permissions in Delhi?
faqs.a: We guide the process and share the vehicle and crew details your RWA asks for; the gate pass itself is applied for by the resident, usually 24–48 hours before move day. For CGHS societies in Dwarka and Rohini, this is routine and quick.

faqs.q: What happens to my move if GRAP restrictions are imposed?
faqs.a: If a GRAP stage bans certain diesel goods vehicles in Delhi, we switch to a compliant CNG/BS-VI vehicle where available or agree the nearest workable date with you — communicated proactively, never on the morning of the move.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay an advance to book in Delhi?
faqs.a: No booking advance is taken. A written quote is shared first, and payment falls due as agreed in that quote — the policy exists precisely because advance-payment fraud is the most common complaint in this industry.

faqs.q: How is my Delhi move insured?
faqs.a: Transit insurance options are explained in the quote, including declared-value cover. Claim terms and exclusions are shared in writing before you confirm — see our charges and terms pages for how coverage is documented.

faqs.q: Can you move a car or bike along with household goods from Delhi?
faqs.a: Yes — cars move on dedicated car carriers and bikes as crated cargo; both can be combined with your household consignment on intercity routes, with separate condition reports at pickup and delivery.

intro: Delhi moves are a logistics puzzle before they are a packing job: peak-hour no-entry windows for goods vehicles, RWA gate passes in the CGHS belt, and colonies where a 32-ft container simply cannot enter. Shiftify plans Delhi moves around the city's rules first — the loading slot, the vehicle size and the shuttle plan are all fixed in the written quote, not improvised on your street.
whyLocal: Delhi punishes improvisation. A truck that reaches your gate at 8 a.m. on a weekday may legally have to wait out the no-entry window; a container routed through a service lane with a height barrier turns a moving day into a standstill. Our Delhi planning starts with the approach: we check the legal loading window for your road, the largest vehicle your colony entry admits, and whether your lane needs the shuttle-tempo stage that Old Delhi, Karol Bagh and Lajpat Nagar pockets routinely do. In the CGHS heartland of Dwarka and Rohini, gate passes are routine but procedural — vehicle numbers and crew lists go to the society office a day or two ahead, and our supervisors come prepared with both. Winter brings a second layer most movers ignore: GRAP stages can suspend whole classes of diesel trucks when Delhi's air turns severe, so October-to-January bookings get compliant vehicles pencilled in from the start. None of this is exotic — but it is exactly the local detail that separates a written quote from a guess, and it is why our Delhi quotes name the loading window, the vehicle class and the shuttle plan line by line.
